findings.title: Mobile menu button cannot be reached or operated by keyboard
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Critical (control not operable by keyboard); it is already the top level, so the critical-path step leaves it at Critical.
findings.user_impact: At widths under 600 px the navigation is hidden behind a <div class="menu-toggle"> with a click listener and no tabindex, role or name, so keyboard users can't open the menu on any page and screen readers don't announce it. On the home page the Book an appointment button in the content is still reachable, so the booking path isn't blocked.
affected_users: Keyboard-only users on small screens or zoomed browsers
findings.remediation: Make the toggle a <button type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="site-nav" aria-label="Menu"> and update aria-expanded when it opens; give the <nav> id="site-nav".
findings.verification_step: At 320x640, Tab to the menu button, press Enter and Space to open and close it, and Tab into the links. axe and IBM should report a named button, and keyboard.unreachable must be empty.

findings.title: Keyboard focus is trapped in the preferred-day picker
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Critical; 2.1.2 is a non-interference criterion, so any failure blocks use of the whole page.
findings.user_impact: Once keyboard focus enters the day picker it cycles through the five day buttons for good: Tab, Shift+Tab and Escape all stay inside (probe: 29 presses, then 8 x Shift+Tab and 8 x Escape). The Request appointment button and everything after it can't be reached, so keyboard and switch users can't book.
findings.remediation: Remove the keydown handler that calls preventDefault on Tab in the .datepicker. If the days should behave as one control, use a radio group (native radios, or role="radiogroup" with arrow-key roving tabindex) so Tab moves on to the next field.
findings.verification_step: Tab from the Mobile field through the day picker to Request appointment and on to the footer; Shift+Tab back out. Re-run run_audit.py: keyboard.trap must be empty for book.html at both viewports.

findings.title: Logo link has no accessible name on every page
findings.severity_rationale: Serious (overridden from Critical): an unnamed link in the header of every page, with a working alternative.
findings.severity_override_reason: The rubric default is Critical for an unnamed functional image, but this link duplicates the Home link in the navigation, so no function is lost; screen readers announce "link, index.html" or just "link".
findings.user_impact: The header logo is a link whose only content is an without alt. Screen readers announce it as an unlabelled link or read the file name, on every page.
findings.remediation: Add alt="Harbour Dental home" to the logo image (the link takes its name from it).
findings.verification_step: axe image-alt and link-name, IBM img_alt_valid and a_text_purpose, and HTMLCS H30.2 pass on all four pages; the accessibility tree shows link "Harbour Dental home".

findings.title: Navigation links have insufficient text contrast
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Serious: primary navigation text below 4.5:1 on every page.
findings.user_impact: The navigation links are #8c9aa6 on #ffffff (2.9:1, needs 4.5:1), on every page and in the open mobile menu. Low-vision users and anyone on a phone in sunlight struggle to read the site navigation.
findings.remediation: Darken nav a to at least #5f6f7a (4.9:1 on white), or reuse the body text colour #1d2b33.
findings.verification_step: axe color-contrast, IBM text_contrast_sufficient and HTMLCS G18 pass for header nav a on all pages at both viewports.

findings.title: Navigation links show no focus indicator
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Serious: keyboard users lose track of where they are in the main navigation on every page.
findings.user_impact: nav a:focus { outline: none } removes the focus ring and nothing replaces it: the focus-visibility probe measured [0] changed pixels around each nav link when focused, on every page and in the open mobile menu. Other controls on the page do show a ring.
affected_users: Low-vision users who use a keyboard
findings.remediation: Delete the nav a:focus rule, or replace it with nav a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0b6e8a; outline-offset: 2px; }.
findings.verification_step: Tab through the navigation; each link shows a visible ring. The probe reports changed_px above half the element perimeter for every nav link.

findings.title: Footer links are hidden under the sticky call bar when focused
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Serious: focused links completely hidden on most pages.
findings.user_impact: When the footer links (Contact, Fees, Privacy) receive focus, the browser scrolls them to the bottom edge of the viewport, where the fixed 64 px call bar covers them completely (9 of 9 sampled points covered, at both viewports, on 3 of the 4 pages; the booking page could not be checked because of the keyboard trap).
findings.remediation: Add padding-bottom: 64px to body (or scroll-padding-bottom: 64px on html) so content can scroll clear of the call bar, or make the bar static at the end of the page on small screens.
findings.verification_step: Tab to each footer link at 1280x800 and 320x640; the focused link is fully visible. focus.obscured must be empty.

findings.title: Button text is clipped with larger text spacing and at 200% zoom
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Moderate for 1.4.12 clipping; one level up because the Request appointment button is on the booking step.
findings.user_impact: .btn has a fixed width of 190 px with overflow: hidden and white-space: nowrap. With the WCAG text-spacing overrides, 13 px of "Request appointment" and 3 px of "Book an appointment" are cut off, and at 200% zoom the submit label loses 0 px. Users who need wider spacing or zoom see truncated labels on the two buttons of the booking path.
affected_users: Users with dyslexia or low vision who override text spacing
findings.remediation: Replace width: 190px; height: 40px; line-height: 40px; overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap with min-width: 190px; padding: 10px 20px; line-height: 1.25 so the button grows with its text.
findings.verification_step: Re-run the text_spacing and resize_text probes; neither reports a.btn or button.btn. Manually apply the text-spacing bookmarklet and zoom to 200%; both labels are readable in full.

findings.title: Footer address text has insufficient contrast
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Moderate: secondary text (address, opening hours) below 4.5:1 on every page.

instances.html_snippet: Harbour Dental, 12 Wharf Street, Sydney NSW 2000. Open Monda…
Harbour Dental, 12 Wharf Street, Sydney NSW 2000. Open Monda…
Harbour Dental, 12 Wharf Street, Sydney NSW 2000. Open Monda…
Harbour Dental, 12 Wharf Street, Sydney NSW 2000. Open Monda…

findings.user_impact: The footer paragraph text is #999999 on #f4f4f4 (2.6:1). It carries the clinic address and opening days.
findings.remediation: Use #5c5c5c or darker on #f4f4f4 (6.1:1), or the body text colour.
findings.verification_step: axe color-contrast, IBM text_contrast_sufficient and HTMLCS G18 pass for footer p on all pages.

findings.title: Form errors are shown only by a red border
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Serious for 3.3.1; one level up because correcting errors is a step of the booking path.

instances.html_snippet: <input id="name" name="name" placeholder="Full name" required="" class="invalid">

findings.user_impact: After a failed submit, the only sign of which fields are wrong is a red border. Screen reader users are not told which fields failed or why, the summary is not announced, and users who cannot distinguish red can't find the errors.
findings.remediation: For each invalid field add a text message ("Enter your full name") linked with aria-describedby, set aria-invalid="true", and move focus to the first invalid field or to a summary with role="alert" that links to each field.
findings.verification_step: Submit the empty form: each invalid field has visible text describing the error, aria-invalid="true", and the message is announced by a screen reader (NVDA or VoiceOver).
findings.resolution: IBM style_color_misuse asked for review of colour-only meaning. In the errors state (submit pressed with empty fields) the screenshot shows only a red border on Full name and Email and the generic text "Please fix the errors below." The DOM adds class="invalid" with no aria-invalid, no per-field message and no aria-describedby; the accessibility tree is unchanged apart from the summary paragraph.

findings.title: Mobile number field has no accessible name
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Serious; one level up because the field is on the booking step.
findings.user_impact: The visible label "Mobile" has for="tel", but the input's id is "phone", so the label is not associated. Screen readers announce an unnamed text field (the accessibility tree shows "textbox" with no name), and clicking the label does not focus the field.
affected_users: Users with motor impairments who rely on the larger label click target
findings.remediation: Change <label for="tel"> to <label for="phone">.
findings.verification_step: axe label, IBM input_label_exists and label_ref_valid, and HTMLCS H91/H44 pass; the accessibility tree shows textbox "Mobile".

findings.title: Full name field is labelled only by its placeholder
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Serious; one level up because the field is on the booking step.

instances.html_snippet: <input id="name" name="name" placeholder="Full name" required="" class="invalid" style="">

findings.user_impact: Once someone starts typing, the field's only label disappears; users with memory or cognitive impairments, and anyone returning to the form after an error, can't tell what the field is for. The placeholder text is also light grey.
affected_users: Users with cognitive or memory impairments
Screen magnifier users who see only part of the form
findings.remediation: Add a visible <label for="name">Full name</label> above the field, matching the Email and Mobile fields, and keep the placeholder only for an example.
findings.verification_step: The field has a persistent visible label; IBM input_label_visible passes; the accessibility tree shows textbox "Full name" with the label as its source.
findings.resolution: IBM input_label_visible flagged the field for review. The screenshot and the accessibility tree confirm the only label is placeholder="Full name": it has an accessible name, but no visible label once text is typed, and the field has no instructions. HTMLCS F68/H91 reported a missing name; that part was dismissed (C-002, C-023) because the placeholder supplies one.

findings.title: Home page carousel moves automatically with no way to pause it
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Critical; 2.2.2 is a non-interference criterion.
findings.user_impact: The carousel advances every 3 seconds forever. The motion probe saw it still changing between 5.0 s and 7.5 s after load and found no pause, stop or hide control; it also keeps moving with prefers-reduced-motion. Users who need time to read, or are distracted by motion, can't stop it.
affected_users: Users with attention or cognitive impairments
Screen reader and magnifier users (content changes under them)
findings.remediation: Add a visible Pause/Play button inside the carousel, pause on hover and focus, and do not auto-advance when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is set.
findings.verification_step: The motion probe finds a pause control for div.carousel, and with reduced motion the carousel does not change.

findings.title: Contact page has an empty title
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Serious: the page has no title at all.
findings.user_impact: contact.html has <title></title>. Screen readers announce no page name, and browser tabs, history and bookmarks show only the URL.
findings.remediation: Set <title>Contact us - Harbour Dental</title>.
findings.verification_step: axe document-title, IBM page_title_exists and HTMLCS H25.1 pass on contact.html.

findings.title: Services page declares German but is written in English
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Serious: screen readers read the whole page with German pronunciation.
findings.user_impact: services.html has <html lang="de">, but the text is English (probe: 39 English stop words against 0 German in 154 words). Screen readers switch to a German voice and the page becomes hard to understand; translation tools may offer to translate it from German.
affected_users: Users of text-to-speech and translation tools
findings.remediation: Change the services page to <html lang="en"> (or en-AU), matching the other pages.
findings.verification_step: The language probe reports lang "en" with detected "en" for every page.

findings.title: Promotion banner forces horizontal scrolling at 320 px
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Serious: the page needs two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px.

instances.html_snippet: Spring offer: a check-up and clean for new patients is $199 …

findings.user_impact: p.promo has width: 760px, so at 320 px the page scrolls horizontally (464 px wider than the viewport) and every line of the offer has to be scrolled sideways to read. People who zoom to 400% on a desktop get the same layout.
findings.remediation: Replace width: 760px with max-width: 760px.
findings.verification_step: At 320x640 the reflow probe reports horizontal_scroll false for index.html.

findings.title: Services page section headings are styled divs
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Moderate: headings are missing from the structure but the text is still readable in order.
findings.user_impact: Screen reader users navigating by heading find only "Services and fees" and can't jump to the Fees section; the page structure exists only visually.
affected_users: Users of reader modes and outline tools
findings.remediation: Change <div class="h2"> to <h2> (keeping the class for styling).
findings.verification_step: The accessibility tree lists heading "General dentistry" [level=2], "Cosmetic dentistry" [level=2] and "Fees" [level=2]; IBM text_block_heading no longer reports them.
findings.resolution: IBM text_block_heading asked whether these blocks are headings. The screenshot shows "General dentistry", "Cosmetic dentistry" and "Fees" in 24 px bold, styled like the h2 headings on other pages; the DOM has <div class="h2"> and the accessibility tree has no headings after the h1.

findings.title: Three "Read more" links have the same text and no context
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Moderate: ambiguous links, but all three go to the same page.
findings.user_impact: In a screen reader's links list the home page offers "Read more" three times, with nothing to tell which service each is about.
findings.remediation: Make each link specific ("More about check-ups", "More about whitening", "More about emergency care"), or add visually hidden text.
findings.verification_step: The links list in a screen reader shows three distinct link names.
findings.resolution: No engine flags this: axe and IBM only check that a link has a name. In the accessibility tree the three links are all "Read more"; each sits in a card after the card's heading and paragraph, but not in the same sentence, paragraph or list item, so none of the WCAG link contexts applies.

findings.title: Booking fields that collect personal data have no autocomplete
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Minor; one level up because the fields are on the booking step.
findings.user_impact: Browsers and password managers can't fill in the fields, and assistive tools that add icons to known field types can't identify them. People with motor or cognitive impairments have to type everything.
affected_users: Users with cognitive or memory impairments
findings.remediation: Add autocomplete="name", autocomplete="email" and autocomplete="tel".
findings.verification_step: The three inputs carry valid autocomplete tokens; axe autocomplete-valid passes.
findings.resolution: No engine checks for a missing autocomplete attribute (axe autocomplete-valid only checks values that are present). Reading the form: name, email and phone collect the user's own details and none has autocomplete.

findings.title: Fees table scroll area is not keyboard focusable in every browser
findings.severity_rationale: Moderate (overridden from Critical): affects some browsers only, and only part of one table.
findings.severity_override_reason: Rubric default is Critical, but Chromium (used for this audit) and Firefox make scroll containers focusable on their own; the keyboard probe reached div.prices. Only browsers without that behaviour (Safari) are affected, and only the last two columns are hidden.
findings.user_impact: At 320 px the fees table scrolls horizontally inside div.prices, which has no tabindex. In browsers that don't focus scroll containers automatically, keyboard users can't scroll to the Health fund item and Usual time columns.
findings.remediation: Give the wrapper tabindex="0", role="region" and aria-label="Fees" so every browser can focus and scroll it.
findings.verification_step: axe scrollable-region-focusable passes; in Safari, Tab to the table and scroll it with the arrow keys.

findings.title: Check-ups help tooltip cannot be dismissed or hovered
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Moderate: the tooltip covers card text but only appears on hover.

instances.selector: body > main > div:nth-of-type(2) > div:nth-of-type(1) > h3 > span:nth-of-type(1)

findings.user_impact: Hovering the "?" next to Check-ups shows a tooltip that stays when Escape is pressed (dismissible: False) and disappears when the pointer moves onto it (hoverable: False), so magnifier users can't read it and it can't be closed to reveal the text underneath. It also never appears for keyboard users, because the "?" is not focusable.
findings.remediation: Show the tooltip on hover and focus of a focusable trigger (a <button> with aria-describedby), keep it open while the pointer is over the trigger or the tooltip, and close it on Escape.
findings.verification_step: The hover probe reports dismissible true and hoverable true; the tooltip opens on keyboard focus.

findings.title: Carousel arrow buttons are too small and too close together
findings.severity_rationale: Rubric default Minor: 18 x 18 px targets 2 px apart; the content is also reachable by waiting.
findings.user_impact: The previous and next buttons are 18 x 18 px and 2 px apart, so a 24 px circle on one overlaps the other. People with tremors or large fingers hit the wrong arrow.
findings.remediation: Make each button at least 24 x 24 px (44 x 44 recommended) or space them so their 24 px circles don't overlap.
findings.verification_step: axe target-size, IBM target_spacing_sufficient and the target_size probe pass for the carousel buttons.

advisories.title: Text below the AAA enhanced contrast ratio (7:1)
advisories.note: Call bar, footer links, buttons and the error summary are between 4.5:1 and 7:1 (for example white on #0b6e8a is 5.8:1). They meet AA; 1.4.6 is Level AAA, above the target.
advisories.remediation: Only if AAA is a goal: darken the teal to #08546a or below.

advisories.title: Call bar and cookie banner sit outside any landmark
advisories.note: axe region and IBM aria_content_in_landmark: screen reader users navigating by landmark skip the emergency phone number and the cookie notice. Not a WCAG failure.
advisories.remediation: Put the call bar inside the footer landmark or give it role="complementary" with aria-label="Emergency contact"; give the banner role="region" aria-label="Cookie notice".

advisories.title: Day picker container is focusable but has no role
advisories.note: IBM element_tabbable_role_valid: <div class="datepicker" tabindex="0"> is a Tab stop announced only as "group" or nothing. Fixing F-2 with a radio group resolves it.
advisories.remediation: Remove tabindex="0" from the container, or give it role="radiogroup" and aria-label="Preferred day".

advisories.title: Check the site in Windows high contrast (forced colours) mode
advisories.note: IBM style_highcontrast_visible is a manual reminder raised for every page with author CSS; the run did not emulate forced colours.
advisories.remediation: Open the site with forced-colors: active (Chromium DevTools rendering emulation) and check buttons, the call bar and focus rings remain visible.

advisories.title: Carousel ignores prefers-reduced-motion
advisories.note: With reduced motion requested the carousel still advances. The WCAG failure is F-12 (2.2.2); honouring the preference is good practice and helps 2.3.3 (AAA).
advisories.remediation: Wrap the auto-advance in if (!matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches).

assisted_review.method: Read the full-page screenshots at both viewports, the errors-state screenshot and the accessibility-tree snapshots (aria/) for every sampled page, and compared the header, footer and call bar across pages.
notes: Agent-judgment findings (F-9, F-11, F-16, F-17, F-18) are kept at medium or low confidence.
Alt text: the only image is the logo (F-3); no image has misleading alt text.
Link purpose: "click here" on the contact page is in the same sentence as "To see the map", so its purpose is clear in context.

limitations: Four pages were audited (the whole example site); templates were grouped by URL pattern and landmark structure.
Only Chromium was used. Keyboard behaviour of scroll containers and media controls differs in Safari and Firefox (see F-19).
The Nu HTML Checker (vnu) did not run, so markup validity (duplicate IDs, invalid ARIA attributes) was checked by axe and IBM only.
No screen reader was used. Announcements (live regions, error messages, carousel changes) were inferred from the accessibility tree, not heard.
The clinic tour video file returned 404 in the audited copy, so captions and audio description could not be checked (NR-1).
The keyboard trap on the booking page stopped the keyboard and focus probes there, so the submit button and footer were not checked by keyboard on that page (NR-2).
Form submission was blocked (allow_form_submission false): the errors state is client-side validation only; server-side error messages were not seen.
Severity is this skill's rubric (RUBRIC.md), not part of WCAG. 21 SCs remain untested and are in the manual test plan.
